blocks.text: The cost of inefficient salary benchmarking

When you handle facilities manager salary benchmarks manually, the costs add up quickly. You face not just the direct cost of labor, but also the hidden cost of errors. If your data is outdated, you risk overpaying or losing talent to competitors who offer more accurate packages. Many managers spend 40% to 60% of their day on administrative chores rather than actual analysis. This prevents you from doing the high-value work that actually impacts your facility operations.

The biggest problem is context switching. You spend your day jumping between Microsoft Excel for Mac, your email, and various compensation platforms. Every time you switch, you lose focus. It takes time to get back into the flow of complex data. Furthermore, relying on static spreadsheets often leads to version control issues. You might be working on a file that lacks the latest salary data for your region or specific industry niche.

items: Inaccurate job matching when comparing titles instead of actual responsibilities.
Using aged data that does not reflect current market shifts.
Manual data entry errors in large Excel workbooks.
Lack of audit trails for pay decisions.

blocks.text: You do not need expensive consultants to fix your benchmarking process. Start by moving to a rolling review model. Instead of a once-a-year scramble, update your data points throughout the year. This makes the process manageable. Use integrated compensation platforms like Pave or Compensation IQ to automate the collection of market data. These tools connect to your HRIS and provide real-time updates that spreadsheets simply cannot match.
Always verify if your benchmarking data is real-time or aged. Using data from two years ago for a 2026 salary decision will lead to significant pay gaps.

faq.question: How do I ensure my salary benchmarking is compliant?
faq.answer: Use software that provides clear audit trails and consistently apply your methodology. Always follow your employer's specific rules regarding the handling of sensitive employee data.

faq.question: Can I do salary benchmarking entirely in Excel?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is prone to error. Use Excel for deep analysis, but pair it with a dedicated compensation platform to ensure your market data is accurate and up to date.
